answer_1.quote: We introduce WebVoyager, an innovative web agent powered by large multimodal models (LMM) that can complete real-world web tasks end-to-end by interacting with websites.
answer_1.outputs: natural language answers to web-based queries, such as prices, flight details, definitions, and summaries

answer_2.quote: We propose an automated evaluation protocol using GPT-4V. Specifically, we save screenshots throughout the online navigation process and then use GPT-4V to evaluate these trajectories together with the final results automatically.

answer_3.quote: We propose to use GPT-4V as an auto-evaluator that emulates the behavior of human evaluators to evaluate the navigation trajectories of WebVoyager.
methods: automatic evaluation using LMM as judge

answer_4.quote: We adopt human evaluation as our main evaluation metric since most of the questions in our benchmark have open-ended answers. In particular, we provide the human evaluators with the complete trajectories of the agent's interaction with the web (all screenshots and all actions), and ask them to provide a binary judgment of whether the agent successfully completed the task.
answer_4.guideline: We ask human evaluators to judge whether the agent successfully completed the task based on the full trajectory, including screenshots and actions. The instruction may involve more than one subtask; failing to complete any subtask should be considered unsuccessful.
